title: Man. Post. Cap. II: similitudes — groan for liberation; tetrum malum called poena
pass_a_gloss: Finally as he who feels the inflicted penalty groans and earnestly desires to be freed from it, so those who seriously detect and acknowledge this corruption in themselves vehemently grieve and bear with difficulty that they are bound by the chains of this evil. For these likenesses that foul and horrible evil deservedly could be called and is called a penalty by many.
pass_b_english: Last likeness: whoever feels a penalty laid on groans and longs for release. Those who seriously find and own this corruption in themselves likewise grieve hard and hate being chained by that evil. For such likenesses many writers have rightly named—and still name—that foul, dreadful evil a penalty.
source_text: Denique ut qui inflictam poenam sentit, ingemiscit, & ab ea liberari percupit; sic qui hanc in se corruptionem deprehendunt & agnoscunt serio, vehementer indolescunt & aegre ferunt se hujus mali vinculis illigari. Has ob similitudines merito tetrum istud & horrendum malum poena dici potuit & dicitur a multis.

choices.choice: Keep groan likeness and multi-author poena naming
